references.text: The prophecy that God sends a messenger in His own name, but the people will not accept him, while they will accept another who comes in his own name.
John comments that many believing leaders loved human glory more than God's glory, which explains why they did not receive Jesus.

Jesus points out earlier in the same chapter that the Father has testified about Him, but they do not have the Father's word in them, underscoring their failure to recognize the one who comes in the Father's name.
Jesus asks why they do not understand His speech, because He comes from God and does not come on His own, yet they refuse to accept Him.
Jesus says that He has done this in the Father's name, but they do not believe in Him because they are not of His sheep.
Jesus warns that all who came before Him were thieves and robbers, and the sheep did not listen to them, contrasting with the one who comes in his own name.
